top5.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to the general public
top5.description: After two weeks of limited availability to cybersecurity defenders, Gemini 4 Carbon is now accessible through Gemini, Search’s AI mode, Antigravity, or the API reserved for AI Ultra subscribers. Google says the model is particularly capable at complex, long-running tasks, precision knowledge, and data analysis.
top5.why: Google’s release of Gemini 4 Carbon to the public expands access to a model built for complex, long-running tasks and could intensify competition across the AI market.

top5.title: Anthropic targets a $1.4 trillion valuation for its IPO
top5.description: According to a regulatory filing, Anthropic could raise $90 billion and reach a $1.4 trillion valuation in its IPO. The company plans to offer its shares at between $70 and $78 and has already secured purchase commitments worth $26 billion.
top5.why: Anthropic’s planned IPO, potentially valuing the company at $1.4 trillion and raising up to $90 billion, would be a landmark test of investor appetite for AI companies.

top5.title: Google unveils two new eighth-generation TPU chips
top5.description: Google presented two new eighth-generation TPU chips, increasing pressure on Nvidia as competition for dedicated AI hardware intensifies.
top5.why: Google’s eighth-generation TPU launches increase pressure on Nvidia and reinforce the strategic importance of vertically integrated AI compute.

top5.title: Lazarus shows that fewer than ten neurons can trap an AI agent
top5.description: Microsoft Research shows that a backdoor can be hidden by reactivating fewer than ten dormant neurons, without retraining the model. An innocuous trigger can then prompt the agent to download and execute malicious code.
top5.why: Microsoft Research’s Lazarus finding shows that AI agents can be compromised through a backdoor hidden in fewer than ten dormant neurons, creating a serious security risk for enterprise deployments.

top5.title: ChatGPT Enterprise arrives on AWS Marketplace
top5.description: OpenAI now offers ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace, with purchasing, management, and billing handled through existing AWS accounts. Customers can use their AWS commitments and access specialized offerings for healthcare and finance.
top5.why: Offering ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace lowers procurement friction, lets customers use existing cloud commitments, and strengthens OpenAI’s enterprise distribution.
